events.title: Fake "Claude Opus 5 Free Desktop" app spreads RevStealer infostealer, researchers say
events.date_note: Help Net Security, dated 2026-09-01, already reports Morphisec research on this RevStealer campaign; the 23 Nov GBHackers and Cyber Security News articles are later coverage. Older than the map window.
events.summary: A fake "Claude Opus 5 Free Desktop" app installs RevStealer, a Windows infostealer, according to GBHackers (citing Morphisec) and Cyber Security News (citing Cyberint). Cyber Security News says Cyberint did not attribute it to a named threat actor. GBHackers says there is no sign Anthropic was compromised, and that Morphisec confirmed it looks for 12 password managers and more than 50 crypto wallets.
events.plain: A fake Claude desktop app installs password- and crypto-wallet-stealing malware. GBHackers says there is no sign Anthropic itself was compromised.
events.exec: Fake AI-app lure can steal saved passwords and crypto wallets from Windows users who run it.
events.action: GBHackers advises downloading Claude only from claude.com/download, and if the fake app was run, treating the system as compromised and rotating passwords from a clean device.
events.impact: Credential and crypto-wallet theft on Windows PCs that run the fake app.

evidence.quote: Morphisec confirmed it looks for 12 password managers and more than 50 crypto wallets.
